name: Naga Waterfall
image_query: Naga Waterfall North Sikkim highway Toong
tagline: A roadside waterfall before Toong on the way to Chungthang
meta_description: Naga Waterfall on the North Sikkim Highway between Mangan and Chungthang: a free stop before the Toong check post. Best months, safety, timings and tips.
summary: The Naga Waterfall is a roadside cascade on the North Sikkim Highway between Mangan and the Toong check post, before Chungthang, roughly 80 km from Gangtok. It is a short, free stop on the drive to Lachung and Lachen. It lies below the protected areas, so no permit is needed to stop, though you must cross Toong by 4:00 pm to go on.
intro: The Naga Waterfall comes down beside the North Sikkim Highway on the stretch between Mangan and the Toong check post, a little before Chungthang. We put it at roughly 80 km from Gangtok and 3 to 3.5 hours by road, though distances here are approximate, and the road conditions vary. We have not found a published height or flow figure for it and give none.

Most visitors see it as a stop on the run to Lachung or Lachen. The water falls over rock and forest in a narrow gorge, and drivers pull over for a few minutes while passengers take photographs and stretch their legs. Flow is strongest during the June to September monsoon and lower from November to March.

The stop is below the Toong check post, so no protected area permit is needed just to pull over. Tourist vehicles must cross Toong by 4:00 pm to carry on to Chungthang, Lachung and Lachen, so keep the stop short, and let your driver decide where it is safe. Slides are common on this stretch. Check current status before you travel.

story.title: A waterfall on a road that gets rebuilt
story.text: We have not found a documented history or origin for the name Naga Waterfall, and we do not repeat unsourced stories about it. What we can give with a source is the setting. The waterfall lies on the stretch of the North Sikkim Highway above Mangan, the same corridor that carries every vehicle to Chungthang, Lachung and Lachen. Wikipedia's article on the 2023 Sikkim flash floods records that the October 2023 glacial lake outburst flood from South Lhonak Lake swept down the Teesta valley, destroying the Teesta Stage III dam at Chungthang and washing away bridges and roads. North Sikkim was cut off for months. This particular waterfall is not named there, and we make no claim about how the flood affected it. What we can say is that the highway here has been rebuilt and repaired, and that travel can be interrupted, which is why we always say check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: A roadside cascade
highlights.text: The water falls over rock into the gorge beside the road, and you can see it from the pull-off. Stay behind the barrier or on the verge, and keep away from the wet rock and the spray.

highlights.title: A break on a long drive
highlights.text: The drive from Gangtok to Lachung or Lachen is long, and this is a convenient place to stop and stretch before the final climb. Many drivers stop here for a few minutes on the way up.

highlights.title: Monsoon and winter flow
highlights.text: From June to September the falls are at their loudest, though slides on the highway can interrupt travel. From November to March they are thinner but the roads are more reliable. Check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: Photography after rain
highlights.text: Clean light after rain, when the water is high and the air is clear, gives the best photographs. Take care with your footing and with traffic at the pull-off.

highlights.title: The Toong clock
highlights.text: The waterfall is before the Toong check post, which tourist vehicles must cross by 4:00 pm. Keep the stop short and ask your driver to watch the time.

how_to_reach.text: Shared North Sikkim tour jeeps to Lachung or Lachen pass the falls, and some drivers stop for a few minutes. You cannot normally book a seat just to the falls. A 2N/3D shared package is about ₹6,500 to 9,000 per person, indicative.

A registered private vehicle from Gangtok takes about 3 to 3.5 hours to the falls, depending on traffic and road work. Ask the driver to stop. The road beyond Toong needs a permit through your registered agent.

Stay a night in Gangtok first. The drive from Bagdogra or NJP to Gangtok takes 4.5 to 5 hours on NH10, longer via Kalimpong or Algarah when NH10 is closed by slides, so a same-day push north would miss the Toong cut-off.

costs: Free, as far as we know
where_to_stay: There are no tourist stays at the falls. Most visitors pass by on the way to Lachung or Lachen, which have better rooms and homestays, or stay a night in Mangan, about 15 to 20 km before it, to split the drive and avoid a rush to the Toong check post. Mangan has simple hotels. For stays in Lachung and Lachen, ask us for current options and prices.
tips: Keep the stop to 10 or 15 minutes, because the Toong check post closes to tourist vehicles at 4:00 pm.
Park well off the road and watch for traffic on blind bends.
Stay away from wet rock and the edge of the gorge.
Carry a rain jacket and a refillable bottle, and take your litter with you.
Ask your driver about slides on the road ahead, and check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: A short stop at the Naga Waterfall
experiences.summary: Pull over at the Naga Waterfall for a quick look and photographs on the way to Chungthang. A free, short break from the road that gives some sense of the gorge you are driving through.
body: The falls come down beside the road in the gorge between Mangan and Toong, and drivers know the pull-off. Step out, look at the water falling over rock and listen to the sound, which is louder after rain. It is a good point for photographs and a cup of tea if a stall is open.

Keep the stop short. The road edge is narrow, traffic does not slow for photographers and slides are common on this stretch. Stay back from the wet rock and the drop, and keep children close. Do not climb on the barrier.

Use your time well. On the way up, leave plenty of margin for the Toong check post, which tourist vehicles must cross by 4:00 pm. On the way down, the stop is a pleasant break before the final run to Mangan. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the stop at the Naga Waterfall?
faqs.a: Ten to fifteen minutes is usual. Drivers keep it short because the Toong check post closes to tourist vehicles at 4:00 pm. On the way down, you have more time. Ask your driver, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee?
faqs.a: As far as we know, no. It is a roadside waterfall. Arrangements can change, so check current status before you travel and ask your driver for the safest place to stop.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go near the water?
faqs.a: We advise against it. The rock is wet and slippery, the flow can rise quickly after rain and the road is narrow with passing traffic. Watch from the pull-off, keep children close and follow your driver's advice.

experiences.title: Planning the day around the Toong cut-off
experiences.best_time: When booking and on the day
experiences.image_query: North Sikkim Highway Toong check post
experiences.summary: Tourist vehicles must cross the Toong check post by 4:00 pm. We explain how to time stops at Singhik, the Naga Waterfall and Chungthang so that a long drive day does not become a race.
body: The Toong check post is the gate between the open highway and the protected areas. As we understand the current rule, tourist vehicles must cross by 4:00 pm. Leaving Gangtok at 9 to 10 am, a car reaches Mangan at lunchtime and Toong by mid-afternoon, so the margin is not large.

Choose your stops. Singhik viewpoint and the Naga Waterfall are each worth 10 to 20 minutes, but not both if you are late. Eat quickly at Mangan, ask your driver to watch the clock and skip a stop rather than risk the cut-off. A night in Mangan the day before removes the pressure entirely.

Landslides and road work can add hours, especially in the monsoon, and the cut-off does not move. If you are behind, the driver may advise turning back. Plan a buffer and an extra night, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the Toong check post cut-off?
faqs.a: Tourist vehicles must cross the Toong check post by 4:00 pm, as we understand the current rule, to go on to Chungthang, Lachung and Lachen. Rules can change, so check current status before you travel and confirm with your registered agent.

faqs.q: What happens if we miss the cut-off?
faqs.a: You would normally have to spend the night below Toong, in Mangan or nearby, and continue the next day, which may disturb your permits and hotel bookings. Plan an early start or a night in Mangan the day before to avoid this.

faqs.q: Can we skip the waterfall if we are late?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should. The stop is a pleasant extra, not a priority. Ask your driver to skip it and Singhik if the clock is tight, and enjoy them on the way down instead.

experiences.title: Mangan, Singhik and the waterfall in one morning
experiences.summary: If you spend a night in Mangan, use the next morning for the Singhik viewpoint, the Naga Waterfall and the road to Chungthang. A relaxed way to see this stretch without racing the Toong cut-off.
body: Wake early at Mangan, and drive about 4 km to the Singhik viewpoint for the first light on Kangchenjunga if the sky is clear. Have tea there, and watch the valley clear as the sun climbs. Return to Mangan for breakfast, then continue north.

The Naga Waterfall lies beyond Singhik, on the road to Toong. Stop for ten to fifteen minutes, take photographs and carry on to the check post, which tourist vehicles must cross by 4:00 pm. With an early start, you reach Chungthang, where the Lachen and Lachung rivers meet, by midday.

This plan needs your registered agent to arrange permits for the day beyond Toong, so tell us when booking. A local taxi for the Singhik and waterfall legs costs roughly ₹1,500 to 2,500, indicative. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a night in Mangan worth it?
faqs.a: It is worth it if you arrive late in Gangtok, travel with older parents or young children over five, or want an easier pace. It splits the drive and removes the cut-off pressure. For a short 2N/3D trip, most people drive straight through.

faqs.q: How far is the waterfall from Mangan?
faqs.a: Roughly 15 to 20 km by road, about 40 to 50 minutes, though we give this as approximate. Landslides and road work can add time. Ask your driver and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can we do this without a permit?
faqs.a: The stops at Mangan, Singhik and the waterfall are below Toong and need no protected area permit for Indian visitors. The road beyond Toong needs a permit through a registered agent. Check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Photographing the falls after rain
experiences.best_time: Morning after rain, June to September and October
experiences.summary: Waterfalls look their best after rain, when the flow is high and the air is clear. We give practical advice for photographing the Naga Waterfall safely, without climbing or standing in the road.
body: A day or two after rain, the flow is high and the colours of moss and rock are saturated. The light is best in the morning, when the gorge is partly shaded and the spray catches the sun. Use a steady hand or a small tripod, and a slow shutter speed if you want the water to blur.

Safety comes before the picture. The pull-off is beside a working road, with blind bends and fast vehicles. Do not stand on the carriageway, and do not climb the wet rock or the barrier for a closer view. Wipe your lens, because spray fogs it quickly.

The monsoon months give the strongest flow but also the greatest risk of slides, so travel only when your driver says the road is clear. Check current status before you travel, and leave if you hear rocks or see water turn muddy and fast.

faqs.q: When is the best light for the waterfall?
faqs.a: Morning, when the gorge is shaded and the spray catches the sun. After rain the flow is high and the colours rich. The monsoon gives the strongest flow, but slides make travel riskier. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I use a tripod?
faqs.a: Only if you can set it up well off the road, on firm ground and without blocking the pull-off. Space is limited and vehicles pass close. A small tripod or a steady rest on the barrier is usually enough.

faqs.q: Is a drone allowed?
faqs.a: We advise against it. The area is close to Army installations and drones draw attention and may break rules. Photography of military areas is not allowed. Check current status before you travel and follow your driver's advice.

faqs.q: Where is the Naga Waterfall?
faqs.a: It is beside the North Sikkim Highway between Mangan and the Toong check post, a little before Chungthang, in Mangan district (North Sikkim). We put it roughly 80 km from Gangtok, about 3 to 3.5 hours by road, and give the figure as approximate.

faqs.q: How tall is the Naga Waterfall?
faqs.a: We have not found a published height and do not quote one. It is a roadside cascade seen from a pull-off, and its flow varies strongly with the season, with the heaviest flow in the June to September monsoon.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to stop at the waterfall?
faqs.a: No protected area permit is needed to stop, as the falls are below the Toong check post. To go on beyond Toong to Chungthang, Lachung and Lachen you need a protected area permit through a Sikkim Tourism-registered agent. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the Toong check post cut-off?
faqs.a: Tourist vehicles must cross the Toong check post by 4:00 pm, as we understand the rule. That is why stops at the falls are kept short. Rules can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee?
faqs.a: As far as we know, no. It is a roadside waterfall. Arrangements can change, so check current status before you travel and ask your driver.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: October to May gives the most reliable roads. Flow is strongest from June to September, but slides are frequent then. Autumn gives a good flow after the rains. Check current status before you travel, in any season.

faqs.q: How long should we stop?
faqs.a: Ten to fifteen minutes is enough for a look and photographs. Longer stops add little, and the road edge is narrow. On the way up, watch the Toong cut-off.

faqs.q: Is the Naga Waterfall safe to visit?
faqs.a: As a short roadside stop, yes, with care. Stay back from the wet rock and the edge, keep children close and watch for traffic. Slides are common on this stretch in the monsoon, so follow your driver's advice and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the waterfall worth the stop?
faqs.a: Yes, as a short break on a long drive. It is free and easy, and gives a feel for the gorge. It is not worth a special trip, and if the clock is tight at Toong, skip it and enjoy it on the way down.
